key_insight: This paper shows that spiking neural networks can be redesigned together with specialized neuromorphic hardware to run much faster and more efficiently. By adding a dual memory pathway, the system achieves over 4× higher throughput, 5× better energy efficiency, and uses 40–60% fewer parameters.
problem_solved: Neuromorphic AI systems often struggle to balance performance, memory usage, and hardware efficiency. This work addresses the challenge of making spiking models both accurate and practical on custom chips.
method: Designs a spiking neural network with two memory pathways to improve temporal processing and compactness.
Co-optimizes the neural architecture with a custom neuromorphic chip rather than treating software and hardware separately.
Demonstrates the resulting system on hardware, showing large gains in throughput, energy efficiency, and parameter reduction versus prior methods.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a path to deploying more capable spiking models on edge and low-power devices. It highlights that algorithm–hardware co-design can unlock efficiency gains that are hard to achieve with model design alone.

paper_title: Algorithm–hardware co-design of neuromorphic networks with dual memory pathways
paper_authors: Pengfei Sun, Zhe Su, Jascha Achterberg, Giacomo Indiveri, Dan F. M. Goodman
